start_phrase: New Brunswick, N.J. (August 30, 2023) – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) (“the Company”) today announced updates to its financials and 2023 guidance which reflect its operations as a company focused on transformational innovation in Pharmaceutical and MedTech.
summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) announced updated 2023 guidance following completion of the Kenvue separation, repositioning J&J as a Pharmaceutical and MedTech company. The company projects Adjusted Reported EPS of $10.00–$10.10 (12.5% growth at midpoint) and Adjusted Operational EPS of $9.90–$10.00 (11.5% growth at midpoint). Johnson & Johnson Announces Updated Financials and 2023 Guidance Following Completion of the Kenvue
Separation
•Company expects increased 2023 Reported Sales Growth of 7.0% - 8.0%, Operational Sales Growth of 7.5% - 8.5%, and
Adjusted Operational Sales Growth of 6.2% - 7.2%; Figures exclude the COVID-19 Vaccine
•Company expects 2023 Adjusted Reported Earnings Per Share (EPS) of $10.00 - $10.10, reflecting increased growth of
12.5% at the mid-point and Adjusted Operational EPS of $9.90 - $10.00, reflecting increased growth of 11.5% at the mid-
point
•Company reduced outstanding share count by approximately 191 million; 2023 guidance reflects only a partial-year benefit
of approximately 73.5 million shares or $0.28 benefit to EPS
•Company secured $13.2 billion in cash proceeds from the Kenvue debt offering and initial public offering and maintains 9.5%
of equity stake in Kenvue
•Company maintains its quarterly dividend of $1.19 per share
New Brunswick, N.J. (August 30, 2023) – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) (“the Company”) today announced updates to its financials and
2023 guidance which reflect its operations as a company focused on transformational innovation in Pharmaceutical and MedTech. The
Company has published a recorded webinar for investors to provide additional context behind the updated financials and 2023 guidance
found in this release, which may be accessed by visiting the Investors section of the Company's website at webcasts & presentations.
“The completion of this transaction uniquely positions Johnson & Johnson as a Pharmaceutical and MedTech company focused on delivering
transformative healthcare solutions to patients,” said Joaquin Duato, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer. “We are incredibly
proud of the focus and dedication of our employees worldwide to achieve this milestone, which we are confident will unlock near- and long-
term value for all of our stakeholders.”
As previously announced, the Company recently completed an exchange offer to finalize the separation of Kenvue Inc., formerly Johnson &
Johnson’s Consumer Health business. As a result of the completion of the exchange offer, Johnson & Johnson will now present its
Consumer Health business financial results as discontinued operations, including a gain of approximately $20 billion in the third quarter of
2023.
Unless otherwise noted, the financial results and earnings guidance included below have been recast to reflect the continuing operations of
Johnson & Johnson.

summary:
- Johnson & Johnson issues updated full-year 2023 guidance (August 2023) excluding Consumer Health, contrasted with prior July 2023 guidance that included Consumer Health (pre-Kenvue separation).
- Key August 2023 outlook (ex-Consumer Health):
  - Adjusted operational sales growth: 6.2%–7.2% (midpoint 6.7%).
  - Operational sales: $83.6B–$84.4B (midpoint $84.0B), up 7.5%–8.5%.
  - Reported sales: $83.2B–$84.0B (midpoint $83.6B), up 7.0%–8.0%.
  - Adjusted operational EPS (diluted): $9.90–$10.00 (midpoint $9.95), up 11.0%–12.0%.
  - Adjusted EPS (diluted): $10.00–$10.10 (midpoint $10.05), up 12.0%–13.0%.
  - Average diluted shares: ~2,557 million.
- July 2023 guidance (including Consumer Health) for comparison:
  - Operational sales: $99.3B–$100.3B (midpoint $99.8B), up 7.0%–8.0%.
  - Reported sales: $98.8B–$99.8B (midpoint $99.3B), up 6.5%–7.5%.

  - Adjusted EPS (diluted): $10.70–$10.80 (midpoint $10.75), up 5.5%–6.5%.
  - Average diluted shares: ~2,631 million.
- Kenvue separation and capital actions:
  - Share count reduced by ~191 million via exchange offer; weighted average reduction of ~73.5 million shares recognized from Aug 23, 2023, adding ~$0.28 to full-year 2023 adjusted diluted EPS.
  - Generated $13.2B in cash from Kenvue debt offering and IPO.
  - Retains a 9.5% stake in Kenvue subject to a 90-day lockup; potential tax-efficient monetization in the next year, with no obligation if market conditions aren’t supportive.
- Dividend: Company will maintain its quarterly dividend of $1.19 per share.

  - Company does not provide GAAP forward-looking measures due to unpredictability of legal outcomes, unusual items, and acquisition-related effects.

- Additional information:
  - A recorded investor webinar provides context on the updated financials and guidance.
  - Notes include illustrative Euro rate usage and share count methodology post-Kenvue exchange.
  - Company overview emphasizes J&J’s mission and role as a diversified healthcare leader.

  - Separates the effects of translational currency and acquisitions/divestitures (including a small Abiomed impact) from reported sales to show operational growth.
  - Key takeaways:
    - WW operational growth remained strong through most of 2022: ~9.1% in H1, ~8.9% through nine months, 6.5% for the full year; Q4 operational growth was roughly flat.
    - U.S. operational growth steady at ~3–4% throughout.
    - International operational growth robust (≈14–15%) for most of the year, with a Q4 dip; heavy currency headwinds meaningfully reduced reported growth vs. operational, especially outside the U.S.

- Segment-level Non-GAAP reconciliations (Income Before Tax from Continuing Operations):
  - For Q1 2023, Q2 2023 (quarter and year-to-date), and each 2022 quarter (Q1–Q4) plus year-to-date and full-year 2022.
  - Reported income before tax and margins for Pharmaceutical, MedTech, and Unallocated, then itemized adjustments to arrive at adjusted income before tax and adjusted margins.
  - Common adjustments include:
    - Intangible asset amortization
    - In-process R&D impairments
    - Litigation-related charges/credits
    - (Loss)/gain on securities
    - Restructuring
    - Acquisition, integration, and divestiture-related items
    - Medical Device Regulation (MDR) costs
    - COVID-19 vaccine-related costs
  - Illustrative results:
    - Q1 2023 adjusted IBT: $7.5B (36.1% margin) vs. reported loss due to large litigation charge in Unallocated.
    - Q2 2023 adjusted IBT: $8.0B (37.2%); 2023 YTD adjusted IBT: $15.5B (36.6%).

  - Periods covered: 2023 Q1, Q2, and first half; 2022 Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, and full year.
  - Reconciles cost of products sold, selling/marketing/admin, R&D, other (income)/expense, interest, restructuring, IPR&D impairments, and taxes to arrive at adjusted net earnings from continuing operations.
  - Tax reconciliations include impacts of:
    - Consumer Health separation tax-related costs
    - Tax legislation and other tax-related items
  - Highlights the impact of large, discrete items (e.g., litigation charges, COVID-19 vaccine-related costs, MDR costs, and securities gains/losses) on GAAP results and how they are removed to reflect underlying operational performance.

- Explanatory note on non-GAAP measures:
  - Defines “Adjusted operational sales growth” as excluding currency and M&A effects.
  - States the intended use (enhance understanding of underlying performance, internal evaluation, planning/forecasting) and limitations (not a GAAP substitute; may reduce comparability to peers).
